failure_modes.name: Natural Language Query Mismatch
failure_modes.trigger: Submitting full conversational questions (e.g. 'dense retrieval failure', 'unsupervised domain adaptation for text embedding models') to lexical/grep tools.
failure_modes.consequence: 0 hits or high false-negative rate because technical codebases use formal class names, variable identifiers, and concise headings.
failure_modes.recovery_strategy: Extract core concept and query the Heading/Structure Index or Regex/Alias Index first.

failure_modes.name: Disconnected Mechanistic Grep
failure_modes.trigger: Grepping for generic library tokens (e.g. 'bm25', 'del_ratio') across all files.
failure_modes.consequence: Returns multiple fragmented code snippets without explanatory narrative, execution output, or parameter context.
failure_modes.recovery_strategy: Anchor the section heading first, then read the contiguous cell block (±5 cells) or query the Pragmatic/Task Index.

failure_modes.name: Lexical Inflexibility
failure_modes.trigger: Exact string matching failing on minor spelling variations (e.g. 'Tranformer-based' typo in Ch 10) or synonym variation ('failure' vs 'caveat').
failure_modes.consequence: Search misses relevant sections despite knowing the conceptual topic.
failure_modes.recovery_strategy: Query the Continuous Semantic Embedding Index or Fuzzy Heading Index with subword n-grams.

failure_modes.name: Jupyter JSON Schema Flooding
failure_modes.trigger: Running unparsed grep directly on raw .ipynb files.
failure_modes.consequence: Results flooded with JSON metadata, base64 image strings, and escape sequences.
failure_modes.recovery_strategy: Always query parsed cell indexes (RepoIndex) or use cell-scoped search tools.
